incident-bot: Pager: high routing error rate detected for /v1/embeddings (sev:P2). Paging @oncall-sre — root: 1772351111

alice: I'm on it. seeing 500s and 'invalid_vector_length' errors hitting us-west embed pool starting 09:12UTC. clients see failed indexing calls.

ben: logs look like responses coming back as text payloads not vectors. here's a snippet from the gateway logs: 
```
2026-03-15T09:12:42Z WARN router: response-type-mismatch org=org-44 route=embeddings.search req_id=abc123 got=chat_text expected=embedding_vector
2026-03-15T09:12:43Z ERROR handlers: vectorize failed invalid_vector_length org=org-44 req_id=abc124
```

carmen: I pushed a routing-policy change earlier (09:05UTC) to relax fallbacks for low-capacity scenarios. config excerpt: 
```
route: embeddings.search
pinned_model: redwood-instruct-v1
fallback_policy:
  allow_cross_type: true
  prefer_same_type: false
```

dmitri: whoa pinned_model is an instruct/chat model for an embeddings route. That explains the text responses. The fallback policy allowed a cross-type fallback when the pinned model wasn't available, and the pinned model itself is wrong for that route.

alice: which customers hit this? I'm seeing 6 orgs affected, highest error-rate at org-44 and org-89. Indexing jobs failing, some production search degraded.

ben: quick mitigation: override routing to force embedding-compatible model. I'm going to apply an org-level override to route to rwd-embed-v2.

ops-bot: applied override: `route_override --org org-44 --route embeddings.search --model rwd-embed-v2 --reason "emergency embed restore"` (applied at 09:30UTC)

alice: monitoring: error rate for org-44 dropped to baseline within two minutes. org-89 cleared by 09:33UTC. overall error count back to <1/min by 09:36UTC.

carmen: I rolled the relaxed fallback globally to reduce failed requests during capacity spikes. I missed validating model-type compatibility for pinned models — policy allowed pinned model that was incompatible with the route. My bad.

dmitri: action items in-thread: immediate rollback of cross-type fallback + validation gate in policy API + add CI to reject model pins where model.type != route.expected_type. I'll open PRs.

ben: temporary guard added: routing-service will reject configs where `pinned_model` model-type != route-type unless `force_cross_type` is explicitly set and flagged. I pushed a patch and hot-restarted routing-service (09:45UTC).

alice: customer comms: Carmen, can you draft an incident note? impact: 6 orgs experienced failed embedding calls and degraded search/indexing for about 18 minutes (09:12–09:30UTC) while pinned-model misconfiguration + permissive fallback policy routed embeddings to a chat/instruct model. No data exfiltration.

carmen: drafting now. high-level message: apology, brief cause, actions taken, and ETA for full postmortem. will link internal postmortem once complete.

ops-bot: Incident status updated -> mitigated at 09:36UTC, resolved at 09:50UTC (postfix checks completed).

alice: quick root-cause summary for the postmortem: 1) config error: pinned_model for an embeddings route pointed to a chat/instruct model; 2) policy gap: fallback allowed cross-type model responses without type validation; 3) rollout timing: relaxed fallback rolled at 09:05UTC and pinned model change (bad pin) took effect at 09:12UTC, creating the window.

dmitri: who's owning the postmortem writeup? assigning to carmen as primary, ben as infra reviewer, and alice for monitoring + customer impact section. Carmen will link the draft in #postmortems.

carmen: will have draft by EOD UTC. immediate mitigations: org-level overrides for affected customers, rollback of global relax-fallback, routing-service validation added. follow-ups: policy API validation, add unit test in config-parser, add alert for route->model-type mismatch.

ben: also adding an automated preflight that, on deploy of routing-policy changes, checks pinned model compatibility against the model catalog. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/routing-policy/pull/542 (internal).

alice: closing notes: paging flow worked, hands-on time ~18m to mitigate, root cause is operational (policy + config) not runtime bug. We'll add a post-incident blameless review.
